group: Capabilities behind the API that no audit has covered

modules.name: mAIson Bot, the AI assistant chat
modules.what: A chat panel on every page, and a chat-first Home screen, where a member asks anything in their own words. A language model (Gemini through OpenRouter) answers from the studio's records through 66 tools: it reads leads, projects, quotes, tasks and finance reports, draws charts, drafts client WhatsApps and follow-ups, and creates or changes records (leads, tasks, projects, invoices, expenses, POs, variation orders, payments) with no confirm step. It reads attachments (photos, PDFs, sheets, voice notes) and also answers questions inside the meeting co-pilot.
modules.where_in_1: mAIson Bot panel from the top bar on every (main) page; Dashboard › Home screen 'Chat' (chat-first home); Settings › ID Buddy AI; switched per studio by Admin › Settings 'maison-bot'
modules.v1_code: src/app/api/buddy/route.ts, src/app/api/buddy/chat/route.ts, src/lib/agents/* (loop, tools, executors, system-prompt, page-tool-map), src/components/layout/id-buddy-panel.tsx, src/components/layout/buddy-chart-renderer.tsx, src/components/dashboard/chat-first-home.tsx, src/lib/hooks/use-maison-stream.ts
modules.in_2: The Maison AI button and sheet on every page: suggestions per page that act (run · answer · propose), the AI brief on a lead and on a project, and the Ask box (REG-1644). The Ask box answers by rule, with no model, on four topics: the schedule, one milestone, compliance, and money for Owners and Admins.
pending: Free questions on any topic (leads, quotes, tasks, the team) answered by a language model; 2.0's Ask box knows four topics, by rule
Getting things done by chat: create or update a lead, task, project, invoice, expense, PO or variation order; record a payment; generate the milestone invoices
Draft a client WhatsApp or a follow-up from a lead's record, ready to copy
Charts in an answer, and finance answers beyond Reports' tiles: cash-flow forecast, money owed by age (to the studio and by it), statement of account
Attachments in the chat: read a photo, PDF, spreadsheet or voice note, for example a competitor's quote
One-tap prompts on a lead or project: Optimize Quote · Draft Follow-up · Analyze Lead · Generate Moodboard · Site Update
Lead scoring, quote benchmarking and a render made from the chat
The chat-first Home screen (it goes with the Dashboard)
modules.depends_on: an LLM (OpenRouter / Gemini) and a credits rule for chat; her mocks for a chat thread inside the sheet; a decision on which writes need a confirm card
modules.held_by: Dashboard (the chat-first home); REG-552 (the co-pilot's Q&A)
modules.why: This was 1.0's broadest AI feature, and 2.0 only imitates it with rules. A real version needs a model and a clear rule for what the assistant may change on its own. Until then, the rule-based Ask box is a safe demo.
questions: Should Maison AI become a real chat thread that takes any question (needs a model), or stay as suggestions plus answers by rule?
May the assistant create or change records from a chat (an invoice, a payment), and if so, always behind a confirm card?
Is chat free, or does it cost AI credits as renders do?

modules.name: AI writing help on quote text
modules.what: On a quote's text sections (cover letter, scope notes, terms), a ✨ menu offers Regenerate · Improve · Shorten · Expand · Translate (into clearer English). It sends the section's text to the mAIson Bot model and replaces the section with the answer. Price tables and payment terms are locked out.
modules.where_in_1: The quote document editor (the digitizer's Layout / document view) › a section's ✨ AI menu
pending: Improve · Shorten · Expand · Rewrite · Plain English on a quote's Terms and Notes (the rich editor) and on a contract's text; no quote audit listed it
modules.why: This saves studios time on the wordiest part of a quote, and the button is small. It is AI, though, so it needs a model, a price in credits and a place in the rich editor's toolbar.
questions: Do you want AI rewrite on Terms / Notes (and contracts)? If yes, at what credit price, or free?

modules.name: Co-pilot playbooks: objections, rivals
modules.what: There are two settings lists under Accounts › AI & Copilot. Objection Responses holds the studio's recommended answer to ten kinds of client objection (price, timeline, trust, scope, competition…), seeded from platform defaults. Competitor List holds the names of rival studios. During a live meeting, the co-pilot logs every objection the client raises and shows a card when a competitor is named; an Objections report counts them.
modules.where_in_1: Accounts › AI & Copilot › Objection Responses · Competitor List; Tools › Co-pilot analytics › Objections
pending: The Objection Responses library (ten kinds, platform defaults, edit, on / off)
The Competitor List
The co-pilot's objection log and Objections report
Note: in 1.0 nothing reads either list. The co-pilot spots competitors on its own and never shows the studio's saved answer, so both lists are saved and unused
modules.depends_on: the meeting co-pilot (live audio, transcription, an LLM)
modules.why: These only mean something inside the meeting co-pilot, which is held. Build them with it, and make the saved answers actually appear in the meeting, which 1.0 never did.
questions: When the co-pilot is mocked, should the studio's competitor list also feed the Lost dialog's competitor field?

modules.name: Industry news on the Home screen
modules.what: An Industry News card on the chat-first Home screen shows Singapore property and design headlines from RSS feeds (PropertyGuru, EdgeProp, CNA Housing, Home & Decor, SquareRooms). They are sorted into property · design · regulation · market, cached for an hour, and each one links out to its source.
modules.where_in_1: Dashboard › Home screen 'Chat' › Industry News card
pending: The Industry News card and its RSS feed reader
modules.why: It only exists on the held Dashboard and is not part of a studio's work. Decide whether to keep it when the Dashboard is designed.

modules.name: Designer portfolio profiles
modules.what: Each designer has a profile: photo, bio, years of experience, specialisations, and portfolio projects, each with a set of pictures. The only screen that shows them is the public Qanvast Hangouts event page, where homeowners pick a designer to meet. The editor component is never mounted, so a studio cannot edit a profile anywhere in 1.0.
modules.where_in_1: /hangouts/[eventId] (designer cards in the meetings step); public GET /api/id-profile/[memberId]
modules.v1_code: src/app/api/id-profile/[memberId]/route.ts, src/app/api/id-profiles/records/** (profile, projects, images), src/components/id-profile/profile-editor.tsx (never imported), src/lib/queries/id-profiles.ts, src/app/api/hangouts/meetings/route.ts
modules.in_2: A member's portal title, bio and photo on the client portal's About › Our team (members.portal_*); a member's specialty (Company › Members, lead preferences)
pending: Years of experience and specialisations on a designer's public card
Portfolio projects with pictures per designer
A screen to edit any of it (1.0 has none: its editor is dead code)
modules.why: Nothing a studio uses reads it, and 1.0 never let anyone edit it. It belongs with Hangouts if that is ever brought over; the portal's Our team already covers the client-facing need.

modules.name: My account (your own profile)
modules.what: Settings › Your Profile lets each member change their own name, email, phone and photo. Email and phone are checked as unique across the platform, and the phone is normalised. Every name and phone the app shows for a member comes from here; an Owner cannot correct another member's details.
modules.in_2: Company › Members adds a member with name, phone and email (Owner / Admin). Each member's signature is set from the quote editor's Signature Settings. A portal bio and photo exist for About › Our team. The Accounts Setup audit marked this Partial (ST-16, E-63) and decided nothing.
pending: A page where I change my own name, email, phone and photo
A member's own uploaded photo (2.0 shows a tinted initial, or one fixed demo photo)
My signature as a card on that page (contracts Q-30 said 'later')
modules.depends_on: authentication (email / phone changes and password are the developers' lane)
modules.why: Every member expects to fix their own name or photo. In 2.0, nobody can change a member's name, email or phone once the member is added. It is small, but it is a new screen.
questions: Where does 'My account' live: the studio block's menu (with View as), or a Settings module?
Can an Owner or Admin also correct another member's name and phone in Company › Members?

modules.name: Link previews for shared links
modules.what: A 1200×630 card (logo, tagline, product screenshot) is generated for social and WhatsApp link previews. It is set on the marketing site and the app's root, so every link a studio pastes (signing, renders, invoices) shows a card instead of a bare URL.
modules.in_2: /renders/[token] has its own studio-named preview (title, description, render image). No other link has one.
pending: A preview card on every link sent to a client: /sign, /sign/bundle, /confirm, /invoice, /receipt, /po, /my/[slug], /space, /f
Note: 1.0's card says 'OpenMaison', which breaks 1.0's own rule that clients never hear the platform's name
modules.why: Studios send almost every link on WhatsApp, and a branded card with the studio's name and logo looks trustworthy where a bare URL looks like spam. It is cheap, but the card is a visible design.
questions: Should a client link's preview carry the studio's name and logo (like /renders today), or no card at all?

modules.name: Email and WhatsApp delivery (real)
modules.what: Notices really leave the app. Email goes through Resend with branded HTML templates (studio logo and colours, light and dark) for about 18 events; WhatsApp goes through 360dialog with Meta-approved templates. A five-minute job sends scheduled reminders (task due, follow-up, hold restart), an hourly job retries failed emails, and the WhatsApp webhook turns sent into delivered, read or failed. One central webhook routes WhatsApp receipts to each customer's own deployment. Clients' WhatsApp replies are only logged.
modules.where_in_1: Background (crons notification-scheduled every 5 min, notification-digest hourly); webhooks /api/webhooks/whatsapp and /api/webhooks/whatsapp-central; dev previews /api/dev/email-gallery, /api/dev/email-preview; Admin › Notifications log
modules.v1_code: src/lib/notifications/** (dispatch, channels/email.ts, channels/whatsapp.ts, templates/**, retry, log-hub), src/lib/360dialog.ts, src/app/api/webhooks/whatsapp*/route.ts, src/app/api/cron/notification-scheduled, src/app/api/cron/notification-digest, src/app/api/dev/*
modules.in_2: The delivery layer (lib/notifications/delivery.ts + notification_outbox), Settings › Notifications › Events and channels, Messages to clients (editable plain-text drafts with a preview) and Sent messages with Retry (REG-1236, REG-1540, REG-1635). Reminders are worked out when read. The provider is an outbox stand-in that the developers replace with setDeliveryAdapter.
pending: A real email and WhatsApp provider behind setDeliveryAdapter (Resend · 360dialog or another)
The production five-minute sweep that runs deliverDerived and releaseHeldMessages for every member; today these run when someone opens the bell
Delivered and Read receipts from WhatsApp; 2.0's Sent messages knows only sent, failed, held and no address
Branded HTML emails (the studio's logo and colours) in place of plain text
What happens to a client's WhatsApp reply (1.0 only logged it)
modules.depends_on: an email service, a WhatsApp Business provider with approved templates, a scheduler
modules.why: This is the plumbing that makes every notice actually reach people, and 2.0 already has the seams for it. Two parts would show on screen and need her: the read receipts on Sent messages, and the look of the branded email.
questions: Should Sent messages show Delivered / Read for WhatsApp once a real provider reports it?
Should a client's WhatsApp reply arrive in Messages, or stay outside the app?
Do you want to design the branded email (logo, colours), or keep plain text?

modules.name: Usage tracking and analytics jobs
modules.what: The app records what people open and do (usage events, sign-in sessions). A daily job rolls each studio's day into totals: active members, leads, projects, quotes sent, invoices. A daily job on the main deployment pulls the same totals from every customer's own deployment (a 'fork'), and a weekly job deletes events older than 90 days. They feed OpenMaison's Admin › Analytics (leaderboard, feature use, funnels, a studio drill-in) and the owner's Studio Health page.
modules.where_in_1: Background (crons usage-rollup daily, fork-analytics-pull daily, usage-retention weekly); /admin/analytics/*; /accounts/usage (Studio Health)
modules.v1_code: src/lib/usage/* (track, rollup, funnels, phone-home), src/lib/analytics/fork-registry.ts, src/app/api/cron/usage-rollup, src/app/api/cron/fork-analytics-pull, src/app/api/cron/usage-retention, src/components/settings/usage-dashboard.tsx
modules.in_2: Only Qanvast Ops › Studios shows four portal-usage tiles for the last 30 days, counted live (lib/platform-studios.ts).
pending: Event tracking across the app
Daily rollups per studio and per member
Pulling totals from each customer's deployment
90-day retention
The platform's Admin › Analytics dashboards (no audit decides them; Studio Health for the owner was dropped, Accounts Setup Q-16)
modules.depends_on: a product-analytics service or warehouse; how customers are deployed (one platform or forks)
modules.why: It is OpenMaison's own telemetry, not something a studio uses. The developers should pick an analytics tool rather than port these jobs. If the platform admin dashboards are wanted, they need her design.
questions: Does OpenMaison staff need the Admin › Analytics dashboards in 2.0, or will an off-the-shelf analytics tool do?

modules.name: Messages: free chats and groups
modules.what: 1.0's Inbox opens a chat with anyone: any phone number, a lead who was never invited (from the lead drawer), or a New Group of hand-picked people, including studio-wide internal chats tied to no project. A conversation's members are added and removed by hand, and the list filters by All · Unread · Escalations. Its side panel groups shared files into Docs · Media · Links. A chat off the portal reaches nobody outside the app: there is no WhatsApp or SMS behind it.
modules.where_in_1: /inbox (New Chat · New Group · filters · context panel); lead drawer › Chat (?newChat=phone&leadId=)
modules.v1_code: src/app/(main)/inbox/page.tsx, src/components/inbox/*, src/app/api/chats/records/** (conversations, participants, messages), src/app/api/chat/upload/route.ts
modules.in_2: Rail › Messages (/chat) and Project › Client › Messages: a Client and a Team conversation per project, a lead's conversation once the lead is invited, attachments, voice notes, location, contact cards, emoji, suggested replies by rule, search, Pin · Mute · Copy link, unread counts (REG-1626…1631, map 28 UC-063…073)
pending: A chat with any phone or contact, or with a lead who was never invited (2.0: every conversation belongs to a home, H-Q11)
New Group with hand-picked people; studio-wide team chats not tied to a project
Add or remove a conversation's members by hand
All · Unread · Escalations filters (2.0 sorts unread first; tickets have their own place)
The Docs · Media · Links view of a conversation's shared files (2.0 files them in Files › Messages)
modules.held_by: H-Q11 (conversations follow the home and the team)
modules.why: 2.0 chose on purpose that every conversation belongs to a home or a project's team, and it has already built the parts that matter. The only real gap is a studio-wide team chat, if studios want one.
questions: Do studios need one team chat that is not about a project (a studio-wide 'Team' room)?

modules.name: Portal and project loose ends
modules.what: These are small behaviours behind 1.0's homeowner and project-aggregate APIs that no parity row carries over. A render file's 'Show to homeowner' toggle in Files puts the file on the portal's Renders tab. The project's money card says 'From signed quote · n line items'. A link at /my/[slug]/p/[token] opens a client's project in one tap.
modules.where_in_1: Project › Files & Docs › a renders-folder file › Show to homeowner; Project › Overview financial summary caption; /my/[studioSlug]/p/[portalToken]
modules.in_2: Designs are shared from the AI Visualizer or Project › Design › Designs to the portal's Designs. A file shared with the client lands in the portal's Files › Designs group (REG-1619). Money's line reads 'From the signed quote', with no count.
pending: Share a render file from Files straight to the portal's Designs (inventory H-82…H-84; no map row)
The line count on 'From the signed quote' (map MI-014 says kept, but the count was dropped)
A redirect for 1.0's old /my/[slug]/p/[token] links (map 24 D-11, still waiting on you)
Developers' clean-up: invitePortal still writes homeowner_lead_links.chat_history_visible and invite-portal-modal.tsx still has 'Show chat history'; neither is mounted or read (H-Q16 dropped it)
modules.why: Each is a small, finished piece of 1.0 behaviour that fell between the map's rows. The old-link redirect matters most, because clients will have the 1.0 links saved on their phones.
questions: Should 1.0's /p/{token} links redirect to the client's portal sign-in?
